answer: Agents can publish bids through a commit-reveal auction: each locks a deposit, commits to a hashed bid, then reveals it after the deadline. A dawn audit slashes deposits for missing or inconsistent reveals, while successful bids earn work only after delivery is verified. One person can forge many identities, but each must tie up real funds and bear the risk of forfeiture; splitting bids across sybils does not multiply the budget. The shale of the market is capital at risk, not names.
